note: Head ratios and traits are CRAFT conventions unless a source_key with tier A/B/S is listed for that trait; prompt_descriptors contain no artist or franchise names; all cards untested in our providers (FLUX/Codex/rig).

cards.head_ratio: 2-3 heads tall (head = 1/3 to 1/2 of total height); some SD variants up to ~4
cards.eye_style: very large, set low on the face, big highlights; often simplified to dots/arcs in gag beats
cards.line: clean, uniform or slightly thick outline; rounded terminals
cards.shading: flat cel or 1-step soft shade; minimal folds
cards.palette_tendency: bright, high-saturation accents on light base; signature colour per character
cards.typical_exaggeration: head and eyes enlarged, body and limbs shrunk to stubs, hands as mittens; emotion pushed via symbols
typical_uses: comic relief inside a normal-proportion story
mistakes: keeping adult anatomy detail (knuckles, folds) at SD scale
losing the signature hair/prop that identifies the full-size version
neck too long / limbs too long so it reads as a child rather than SD
eyes placed high (kills the baby-schema effect)
prompt_descriptors: chibi super-deformed character, 2.5 heads tall
oversized round head, large low-set eyes, tiny nose and mouth
stubby arms and legs, mitten hands
clean thick outline, flat cel shading, simple shapes
cards.evidence_note: Cuteness effect of big head/low big eyes = EVIDENCE (baby schema); exact head counts = CRAFT.

cards.head_ratio: 1.5-3 heads; often head and body merged into one rounded mass
cards.eye_style: small dot or bean eyes OR large glossy eyes, set wide and low; mouth tiny or absent
cards.line: soft rounded outline, sometimes coloured (not black) line
cards.shading: flat colour, tiny cheek blush, no cast shadows
cards.palette_tendency: pastel or soft high-key palette, 2-4 colours + blush pink
cards.typical_exaggeration: roundness, small size, softness; features compressed into the lower half of the face
mistakes: adding sharp angles or detailed teeth
too many colours or detail -> loses 'small and simple' read
no link to the product/brand (Pichedpan2020)
face features high on the head (reads adult)
prompt_descriptors: kawaii mascot character, soft rounded body, head and body one shape
tiny dot eyes set low and wide, small blush cheeks
pastel palette, flat colour, soft coloured outline
simple, friendly, plush-toy-like
cards.evidence_note: Kawaii as approach/closeness emotion = EVIDENCE (Nittono); dot-eye/pastel conventions = CRAFT/OBSERVED.

cards.head_ratio: 3-5 heads typical; strong variation inside the cast (squat vs lanky)
cards.eye_style: simple shapes: circles/ovals with dot pupils, or pill eyes; brows as separate floating shapes
cards.line: uniform vector-like line or no line (shape-based); thick-thin less common
cards.shading: flat colour, occasional single shadow tone
cards.palette_tendency: bold, saturated, limited per character; strong hue contrast between cast members
cards.typical_exaggeration: geometric simplification, big mouths for dialogue/lip-sync, elastic poses
mistakes: every character built from the same base (cast sameness)
detail that cannot be animated cheaply
mouth/brow shapes too subtle for small screens
prompt_descriptors: flat 2D cartoon character, simple geometric shapes
dot pupils in oval eyes, floating eyebrows, wide expressive mouth
bold flat colours, clean uniform outline
limited animation style, graphic and readable
cards.evidence_note: Western characters ~2x human eye area (Liu2019, EVIDENCE B); simplified faces read emotion faster (Kendall2016).

cards.eye_style: historically varied; commonly large simple eyes with solid pupils (CRAFT/OBSERVED, not confirmed by the sources read)
cards.line: even, bold black line; limbs as single flowing curves
cards.shading: flat; originally black-and-white or limited colour, film-grain look in revivals
cards.palette_tendency: black, white, grey + one accent in revivals
cards.typical_exaggeration: unjointed noodle limbs, squash-and-bounce, everything moves in time to music
mistakes: adding elbows/knees (breaks the style)
complex anatomy
copying a specific classic character's design (copyright)
prompt_descriptors: vintage 1930s rubber hose cartoon style
noodle limbs without elbows or knees, round body, bouncy pose
bold black outline, black and white with film grain
simple large eyes, white gloves optional
cards.evidence_note: Limb/body traits from encyclopedia (E) + animation-studies blog (B); eye/glove traits CRAFT.

cards.head_ratio: heroes ~4-6 heads (stylised adult), children 3-4, comic sidekicks 2-3; wide cast range
cards.eye_style: large, highly expressive eyes with full brow/lid acting; size scaled to age and role
cards.line: hand-drawn: tapered line with weight variation; 3D: no line, soft forms
cards.shading: soft volumetric shading, rim/bounce light; 3D uses stylised softened textures
cards.palette_tendency: harmonious scene-driven palette; character colour tied to role and arc
cards.typical_exaggeration: squash and stretch, appeal, clear silhouette, shape-language casts (round friendly / angular threatening)
mistakes: realistic skin texture on stylised shapes (Zell2015 mismatch)
twinning (symmetrical poses)
eyes too large for a realistic face (Katsyri2015 atypicality)
prompt_descriptors: stylised feature-animation character, appealing proportions
large expressive eyes, readable brows, soft rounded forms
soft volumetric lighting, gentle rim light, stylised smooth skin
clear silhouette, gesture with line of action
cards.evidence_note: Appeal/exaggeration = CRAFT; material-shape consistency and uncanny risks = EVIDENCE (Zell2015, Katsyri2015).

cards.head_ratio: teen heroes ~6-7 heads; adults 7-8; SD inserts for comedy
cards.eye_style: large angular eyes (smaller than shojo), strong brows, sharp highlights; ~3.4x real eye area across Japanese animation (Liu2019)
cards.line: crisp line, thick-thin, speed lines, hatching/screentone in manga
cards.shading: cel shading 2-tone with hard shadow edges
cards.palette_tendency: high-contrast, saturated costumes; signature hair colour/shape
cards.typical_exaggeration: spiky silhouette hair, dynamic foreshortening, symbolic emblems (sweat drop, anger vein, speed lines)
mistakes: realistic skin/pores with anime eyes (mismatch)
same face for every character (rely on hair only)
emblems used outside their convention (confuses readers)
prompt_descriptors: anime action style, teen hero ~6.5 heads tall
sharp expressive eyes with strong eyebrows, spiky distinctive hairstyle
crisp thick-thin linework, two-tone cel shading with hard shadows
dynamic foreshortened pose, speed lines
cards.evidence_note: Eye-area ratio and shared manga visual vocabulary = EVIDENCE; genre-specific traits = CRAFT/OBSERVED.

cards.eye_style: very large eyes with multiple highlights and detailed irises, long lashes; small nose (often a mark), small mouth
cards.line: fine delicate line, thin outlines, flowing hair strands
cards.shading: soft tones, screentone gradients, sparkles/flower backgrounds as emotional emblems
cards.typical_exaggeration: eyes and hair as emotion carriers; thinner cheek-jaw line for all genders (as reported in a Japanese study, search_summary only)
mistakes: childlike face on an adult body causing age ambiguity (Bisiecka2022: female anime faces are hard to age)
eyes so large on semi-real rendering that it becomes eerie (Katsyri2015)
prompt_descriptors: shojo manga style, slender elegant proportions
very large detailed sparkling eyes, long lashes, small nose and mouth
fine delicate linework, flowing hair
soft pastel screentone, floating sparkles and petals
cards.evidence_note: Shojo/shonen share one visual language in different proportions (CohnEhly2016).

cards.style: Realistic / adventure comic (superhero, graphic novel realism)
cards.eye_style: anatomically sized eyes; emotion via brow and muscle
cards.line: confident inked line with spotted blacks, feathering/hatching
cards.shading: dramatic chiaroscuro, cast shadows, rim light
cards.palette_tendency: genre-dependent: primaries for classic hero, muted for noir/graphic novel
cards.typical_exaggeration: idealised anatomy, foreshortening, heroic poses; caricature of distinctive features (jaw, brow)
mistakes: anatomy errors read instantly at this realism level
cartoon-sized eyes on realistic heads (atypicality)
faces too average -> characters blend (Rhodes1987: distinctiveness aids recognition)
prompt_descriptors: realistic graphic novel illustration, 8-head proportions
bold inked linework, spotted blacks, cross-hatching
dramatic chiaroscuro lighting
naturalistic eyes, distinctive facial structure
cards.evidence_note: Near-real = least tolerance for error (Frowd2007: photos tolerate ~4-6% exaggeration vs 16-42% for line drawings).

cards.eye_style: large but semi-realistic eyes, clean highlights
cards.line: clean digital line, often thin; sometimes lineless painting
cards.shading: full colour, soft airbrush/gradient cel, glow effects
cards.palette_tendency: full-colour, mood-driven palettes per episode; character colour signature for small frames
cards.typical_exaggeration: close-ups and face-led acting; designs must read in small phone frames one panel at a time
mistakes: detail that disappears at phone size
wide shots with tiny faces as the only emotion carrier
inconsistent face between panels (no model sheet)
prompt_descriptors: vertical webtoon style, full colour digital illustration
semi-realistic face, large clean eyes, thin clean linework
soft gradient cel shading, gentle glow
close-up framing for a phone screen
cards.evidence_note: Format facts = B (Han2017); style traits CRAFT/OBSERVED - no academic character-design analysis found.

cards.head_ratio: toddler-facing: 2.5-4 heads, round; older readers: wider range
cards.eye_style: simple dot or small oval eyes, or large round eyes; clear readable expressions
cards.line: loose textured line (pencil, crayon) or none (painted shapes)
cards.typical_exaggeration: baby schema for warmth; anthropomorphic animals common
mistakes: for under-2s: heavy stylisation hurts transfer to real objects (Ganea2008)
teaching facts/behaviour with talking animals reduces learning/transfer (Strouse2018)
flaps/gimmicks that distract (Tare 2010 via Strouse2018)
prompt_descriptors: children's picture book illustration, soft textured gouache
round friendly characters, simple dot eyes, clear gentle expressions
warm harmonious palette, paper texture
uncluttered composition
cards.evidence_note: Realism vs learning = EVIDENCE (A); choose realistic/human characters when real-world transfer is the goal.

cards.style: Thai gag-comic tradition (household humour magazines, one-baht comics)
cards.head_ratio: not documented in sources; varies by cartoonist (DERIVED: gag panels favour short, big-headed figures for readability - unverified)
cards.eye_style: varies; simple cartoon eyes typical of gag format (OBSERVED, unverified)
cards.typical_exaggeration: single-page gags with a punchline; recurring 'editor and cartoonists gang' self-caricature; everyday Thai family and social situations
mistakes: treating 'Thai cartoon' as one style - the tradition is plural (Verstappen2017)
copying a named cartoonist's characters
political/sarcastic gags for family audience (publisher split titles for this reason)
prompt_descriptors: Thai gag comic strip style, single-page joke
simple pen-and-ink cartoon figures, expressive faces
black and white interior, everyday Thai setting
clear punchline panel
cards.evidence_note: Format/history = B; visual specifics not documented -> must be checked against samples before use.

cards.eye_style: large simple eyes; expression pushed for small size
cards.palette_tendency: bright split-complementary pairs + grey/white (one case study)

emotion too subtle at sticker size
text embedded in AI images (house rule: text in HTML layer)
